clinical_features.symptoms:
CLINICAL FEATURES 
*Sudden onset of headache 
*Unusual headache for patient 
*Sentinel headache (40%) 
*Transient or persistent LOC 
*Vomiting 
*Seizures/posturing 
*Meningism 
*Neurological signs ➔ according to area involved 
*Fundoscopy – retinal haemorrhage, papilloedema 
*Risk factors (see box) 
RISK FACTORS 
*Female 
*Age > 50 years 
*Hypertension 
*Smoking 
*Oral contraceptives 
*Alcohol history 
*Connective tissue disease 
*Polycystic kidney disease 
*Family history 
*Coarctation of the Aorta 
*Previous aneurysm/SAH 
 
OTTAWA CLINICAL DECISION RULE OUT 
CRITERIA 
“ANT LEaF” 
A – Age > 40 
N – Neck pain or stiffness 
T – Thunderclap headache 
L – Loss of consciousness (witnessed) 
E – Exertion (onset during) 
and 
F – Flexion (limited neck flexion on examination) 
Patients require investigation if 
one or more findings present
